03 / THE IDEA, WITHOUT THE JARGON

Not smarter ants. Different conversations.

01

An ant tries a route.

“Ant” means one computer-generated round trip. Every stop is visited once before returning to the start.

02

Good routes leave hints.

Shorter routes leave stronger pheromone on their edges. Later ants are more likely to reuse those edges, while still exploring.

03

Change who gets heard.

Instead of one shared trail, the network chooses which earlier routes an ant sees. This can change how useful discoveries spread—and which mistakes persist.

What the paper shows. What this demo tests.

The paper studies an Ising model, not delivery routes. It reports improved success for networks very close to a lattice under its experimental settings. Here, we adapt the reference network to a routing problem. A gain here is evidence for this implementation and budget, not proof that network ACO always wins.

Read the methodology

All three methods construct the same number of tours, use the same distance heuristic (β = 2), pheromone exponent (α = 1), deposit 1 / route length, and share a pheromone floor of 10⁻⁶. The first 21 tours ignore pheromone. Random streams for route decisions are paired across methods; graph sampling uses a separate stream. No 2-opt, elite reinforcement or optimum route is given to any solver.

Simple ACO is a sequential evaporating Ant System variant with evaporation ρ = 1/20 per ant. Network ACO sums deposits from 20 distinct earlier ants sampled without replacement with weight max(20 + ω × reference count, 0). The first 21 ants form a chronological complete graph. Recent-only uses the previous 20 ants. Reference popularity is not solution quality; shorter routes separately receive stronger deposits.

The network selection follows the paper’s discrete model. Its binary linear decision rule and Boltzmann deposits are replaced by conventional TSP edge choices and inverse-length deposits. This is an adaptation, not a reproduction of the paper’s numerical claims. Equal route counts do not imply equal execution time.
